applies_to: APA 7th edition and near variants: author-initial entry starts, a parenthesised year, DOI-final entries.

reproduces.protects_against: inline-APA recovery reading an edited-book editor list ('In Smith, A. B., & Jones, C. D. (Eds.)') as the start of a new entry

cases.note: The plain case. An edited-book chapter's editor list must not read as a new entry.
cases.text:
Doe, J. (2020). A first article title. Journal of Examples, 1(1), 1-10.

Roe, R. (2019). A chapter about things. In Smith, A. B., & Jones, C. D. (Eds.), The handbook of examples (pp. 30-55). Academic Press.

Young, Y. (2021). A third article. Journal of Methods, 3(2), 100-120.

reproduces.protects_against: the line-start APA heuristic splitting a wrapped editor list away from its chapter entry

cases.text:
Baker, S. U. (2020). A chapter on sleep. In Smith, A. B., Jones, C. D., & Brown, E. F. (Eds.), The handbook (pp. 1-20). Press.
Carter, V. W. (2021). Another article. Journal, 2, 20-30.

cases.note: Partial flattening: recovery must re-split only the stuck block.

cases.note: A corporate author opens with neither a surname pattern nor a number, so it precedes every detected start. Losing it drops a reference outright.
cases.text: World Health Organization. (2020). Global report on health. WHO. Doe, J. (2019). An article title. Journal, 1, 1-10. Roe, R. (2021). Another article title. Journal, 2, 11-20.

cases.note: Wrapped page ranges and years leave lines that look numbered. They must not hijack the split.

cases.variant: APA, flattened, no years at all
cases.round: known limitation, resolved in review round 5 (C6)
cases.note: Recorded as a known limitation while the year gate accepted only a literal year: with every entry carrying "(n.d.)" the gate never opened and the block stayed unsplit. Resolved by treating a no-date marker as filling the same slot a year fills. The case was written to be updated when that happened, and this is that update — the expectation moved from 1 entry to 2 because the new behaviour is correct, not to make a test pass.
cases.text: Doe, J. (n.d.). A first untitled resource. Example Press. Roe, R. (n.d.). A second untitled resource. Example Press.

cases.variant: APA, DOI-final entry followed by a corporate author
cases.note: Markdown cleanup collapsed a real blank line here: the previous entry ends in a bare DOI (APA adds no closing period) and the next starts with a corporate author, which matches none of the entry-start markers. The second reference was deleted before splitting ever saw it.
cases.text:
References

Smith, J. (2020). A first article title. Journal of Examples, 1(1), 1-10. https://doi.org/10.1000/xyz123

World Health Organization. (2021). Global report on something measurable. WHO Press.

Young, Y. (2019). A third article. Journal of Methods, 3(2), 100-120.

cases.variant: APA title quoting a term after a comma
cases.note: The quoted-title rule's lookbehind only rejected quotes not preceded by a comma. An APA title that quotes a term after a comma matched it, and because the quoted rule runs first it beat the year-parenthetical rule that would have been right.
cases.raw: Smith, J. (2020). Rethinking replication, "researcher degrees of freedom" and beyond. Psychological Science, 31(4), 400-415.

expect.title: Rethinking replication, "researcher degrees of freedom" and beyond

cases.variant: APA, one entry per line, no years at all
cases.note: Twelve complete one-line entries, none carrying a year. The author-start heuristic waits for a year before closing an entry, so it closed only when the line cap was hit and produced two arbitrary eight-line chunks. '(n.d.)' fills the same slot a year does and now counts as one.

cases.note: The counterpart to apa-doi-final-then-corporate-author. That one covered the link-end half of entry_is_complete; this covers the sentence-end half, on the same shape of input, so neither half can be removed unnoticed.
